title: Grove keeps fully specified Instances Active with all limits set to zero rather than deleting them
content:
The Maple syrupUSDC Instance sits under a heading stating that Instances "with `Active` Status are stored herein," and it carries a complete configuration: token address, underlying asset address, an inflow RateLimitID (`0x99a69e57…`), and a Max Exchange Rate call. Yet A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.13.1.2.4.1 sets deposit `maxAmount`: **0** and `slope`: **0**, A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.13.1.2.4.2 sets withdrawal `maxAmount`: **0**, and A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.13.1.2.5.2 states "the Maximum Exposure for this Instance is **0 USD**."

Zero is doing something a deletion could not. Removing the Instance would discard the ratified addresses, the risk assessment, and the role mappings — all of which would have to be re-approved before Grove could ever use the venue again. Zeroing the limits retains that approved scaffolding while making the conduit economically inert.

The result is a third state between "approved and in use" and "not approved": **pre-cleared but closed**. Restarting the allocation becomes a single parameter change against configuration that has already passed review, which is materially faster than a fresh approval — and materially less scrutinised.

That is the trade-off worth naming. Dormant-but-Active Instances are a standing inventory of venues Grove can re-enter cheaply. It makes the response to a returning opportunity fast, at the cost that the review which authorized the venue may be arbitrarily stale by the time the limits are raised again. A reader auditing Grove's real risk surface must therefore read the rate limits, not the Instance list — the list overstates what is live, and understates what could become live quickly.
description: Maple syrupUSDC retains addresses, RateLimitIDs and Covered risk status while carrying maxAmount 0 and Maximum Exposure 0 USD, so reactivation needs only a parameter change, not re-ratification.
